Dear Dr. Bennett,

Thank you for evaluating Chloe Harris, a 16-year-old female whom I recently saw for a routine health maintenance visit. She has no significant past medical history, takes only a daily multivitamin, and is active in her school band.

On examination, Chloe is notably tall for her age, tracking well above the 98th percentile; her stature is symmetric and proportionate without disproportionate limb lengthening, and short stature has never been a feature. She demonstrates strikingly long, thin digits and marked laxity throughout her peripheral joints, though full extension at both elbows is completely preserved. Her spine exhibits a noticeable lateral thoracolumbar curve on forward bending. The thorax is symmetric, with a neutral chest wall showing no sternal depression or protrusion. Her skin displays normal elasticity without cutaneous stiffening or striae. Her feet show well-preserved arches with no pes planus, and abdominal palpation revealed no groin herniation.

Craniofacial inspection shows a normal skull contour lacking cranial elongation, preserved cheek projection without malar flattening, and normally positioned eyes that are not deeply set. Intraoral exam revealed a steep, high-arched palate along with significant dental crowding. Her recent optometric assessment documented marked nearsightedness and bilateral subluxation of the crystalline lenses; dilated examination confirmed the retinas are intact with no detachment, and there was no lens coloboma. Her cardiovascular and pulmonary examinations were entirely unremarkable.

Given this constellation of findings, I would appreciate your comprehensive assessment and recommendations regarding ongoing monitoring.

Sincerely,
Dr. Laura Sterling
